title: Crypto lesson 2: what a blockchain is

linkedin.media_title: Crypto lesson 2: what a blockchain is
linkedin.text:
"Blockchain" gets used everywhere, but most explanations lose people in the first sentence. Lesson 2 of 100 in crypto from zero.

Start with something familiar: an ajo group. The group keeps one record book of who paid, how much and when. The weakness is obvious. One person holds the book, so one person can change it.

Now give every member an identical copy. If someone edits theirs, everyone else's copy disagrees, and the edit is rejected.

A blockchain is that idea run by thousands of computers worldwide:

1. Each page of records is a block.
2. Each block carries a fingerprint of the block before it, so they form a chain. Change an old page and every page after it breaks.
3. New pages are added by computers that put something at stake. On Bitcoin, miners spend computing power. On Ethereum, validators lock up coins as a deposit. Cheating costs them money.

No single owner. No single point to cheat.

Homework: explain it to a friend using only the record book example. If they get it, you do too.

Education, not financial advice.
